answer: Each PoA identity must complete a prescribed chain of modular squarings, whose next value depends on the previous one; a Wesolowski proof lets peers check the result efficiently, not skip the work. An attacker may run separate chains on multiple GPUs, but cannot parallelize any one chain to erase its sequential delay, so creating many clones imposes a proportional hardware-and-time cost. The violet, ivory, and shale labels do not alter this bound.
